correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact closed neighborhoods \(N[a_i]=\{a_i\}\cup(B\setminus\{b_i\})\) and \(N[b_i]=\{b_i\}\cup(A\setminus\{a_i\})\). If a mixed sequence changes sides after one heavy-side vertex, at most four moves are possible; if it changes after at least two, the first light-side vertex dominates every still-unselected heavy-side vertex except its matched partner, so at most one heavy-side vertex and one terminal light-side vertex can follow. This gives the upper bound \(n\) and forces the four equality types. The counting formulas follow from disjoint parameter choices. The standalone checker independently reconstructs neighborhoods and all legal orders for \(5\le n\le7\).

value.rationale: The result is a natural exact extremal classification for a canonical matching-deleted complete bipartite family. It goes beyond the scalar Grundy domination number by identifying every maximum set, every permissible ordering, and two closed enumerators. The formulas show precisely how deleting one perfect matching creates mixed-side extremizers that are absent in complete multipartite graphs, so the statement captures a structurally meaningful sensitivity rather than a routine recomputation.
